quickAnswer: Chelmsford leans on natural gas more than any of the 50 towns we serve: 76.1% of occupied homes use it, and only 9.6% burn oil. Fuel oil sits at the opposite end, the lowest share of all 50.
body: ## The gas-heated town of the 50

According to the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS), utility gas heats 10,291 occupied homes in Chelmsford, or 76.1%. No other town on our list leans on gas harder. Fuel oil is at the opposite end: 1,303 homes (9.6%), the lowest share of all 50, while the middle town sits at 36.5%. Electricity heats 1,354 homes (10.0%) and bottled gas 349 (2.6%).

In a town where oil dominates, the replacement debate is usually oil against gas. Here gas is simply the default, so the questions shift. Which gas system suits the house, and would a heat pump carry part of the load? The roughly one home in ten that still burns oil is the exception.
## Built fast along Route 3

Wikipedia notes that Chelmsford grew sharply between 1950 and 1970, at the same time U.S. Route 3 was connected in Lowell to Route 128 in the 1950s and then extended up to New Hampshire in the 1960s. The median Chelmsford home was built in 1967, and 5,123 homes (36.7%) date from 1960 to 1979, the biggest single band. In total, 9,511 homes (68.1%) were built before 1980, the 8th-highest share of the 50 towns. Almost nothing is new: just 524 homes (3.8%) went up in 2010 or later, 48th of 50.

Houses from the postwar decades can have ductwork that is undersized or leaky and attics with little insulation by current standards. A new gas furnace sized to the old one can end up too large once the windows and insulation have been improved.
## One home in five sits in a large building

Chelmsford is not only single-family streets. Buildings with five or more units hold 2,834 homes (20.3%), and all multi-unit buildings together hold 3,524 (25.2%), well above the 16.1% of the middle town. Another 339 homes are in two-family buildings and 351 in buildings of three or four units. Detached houses account for 9,483 homes (67.9%), townhouses for 776 and mobile homes for 182.

Larger buildings change the work. A condominium or apartment complex may have one boiler plant or a separate furnace or heat pump for each unit, and the person who calls us may be an owner, a board or a property manager. Renters live in 2,336 households (17.3%). That is a little above the 16.4% of the middle town.
## Villages with their own character

Wikipedia describes a town center plus South, West, East and North Chelmsford and the Westlands, with North Chelmsford an industrial village that has many of its own town services. The town is 25 miles northwest of Boston, borders Lowell to the northeast and is bounded by the Merrimack and Concord rivers. Winters are cold, windy and snowy, and summers warm and humid, so heating and cooling both matter. Chelmsford was incorporated in May 1655, and the growth between 1950 and 1970 explains why the housing is far younger than the town.
## Electric service and rebates

National Grid serves Chelmsford, according to its Massachusetts Electric Company territory list. Mass Save heat pump rebates have conditions that depend on the utility and the home. The figures behind the 2026 heat pump rebate are collected on the [heat pump page](/cities/chelmsford/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Is natural gas the normal heating fuel in Chelmsford?
faq.a: Yes. Utility gas heats 76.1% of occupied Chelmsford homes, the highest share among the 50 towns we serve. Oil heats only 9.6%. A main is not guaranteed on every street, so confirm yours before planning a conversion.

faq.q: Why are so many Chelmsford homes from the 1960s and 1970s?
faq.a: The town grew quickly between 1950 and 1970, as Route 3 was linked to Route 128 and then extended toward New Hampshire. The median home dates to 1967. Houses of that age often have older ducts and modest insulation, so system size should be checked, not copied from the old unit.

faq.q: Do large apartment buildings in Chelmsford need different equipment?
faq.a: Often, yes. About 20.3% of Chelmsford homes are in buildings of five or more units, and those may use a central boiler, rooftop equipment or one system per unit. The right choice depends on how the building is piped and metered, so the heating load is assessed before any quote.

faq.q: Who pays for heat in a Chelmsford rental?
faq.a: Chelmsford has 2,336 renter households (17.3%). The state sanitary code (105 CMR 410.201) sets a heating-season floor of 68 F between 7 a.m. and 11 p.m. and 64 F overnight. Unless the lease says otherwise, the landlord is the one paying for that heat. This is general information, not legal advice, and a lease or a dispute deserves real counsel.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Utility gas heats 76.1% of Chelmsford homes, so most replacements are one gas furnace or boiler swapped for a newer one. For the minority on oil or bottled gas, the first question is whether a main is within reach or a heat pump fits better.
body: ## What a heating replacement looks like on a gas-heavy street

Because gas already heats most Chelmsford homes, a replacement is often a gas furnace or boiler swapped for a newer one. Two groups sit outside that pattern: the 349 homes on bottled gas and the households still burning oil. For them, the first question may be whether a gas main is within reach or whether a heat pump makes more sense than another delivered fuel.

The Census also lists 33 homes heated with wood and 74 with no heating fuel. Those are small groups next to 10,291 gas homes, but they are a reminder that a Chelmsford replacement is not always a like-for-like swap.
### Start with the house, not the nameplate

More than a third of the town was built between 1960 and 1979, and a system sized decades ago may not match what the house needs today. Our heating-load assessment comes before the quote, and the answer can come out below the size of the unit being removed.
### Furnace or boiler

- **Forced air:** a furnace needs good ducts. Leaky or undersized runs waste output, so we inspect them before choosing a size.
- **Hot water or steam:** a boiler swap depends on the radiators or baseboard, the piping and the venting.
### Permits and inspection

Gas work is not done when the burner lights. Swapping the appliance brings a permit and a final inspection, and the permit must be pulled by a licensed plumber or gas fitter. At the final visit the inspector looks at venting, gas piping and combustion air.

### Condominiums and rental buildings
The 2,834 homes in buildings of five or more units sit in a different world from the 9,483 detached houses.

About a quarter of Chelmsford homes are in multi-unit buildings, which can mean a shared plant rather than a single-house system. Across the 3,524 homes in multi-unit buildings, the person who calls may be an owner, a board or a landlord.
### Repair or replace

One failed part on a younger unit is a repair job. A cracked heat exchanger, or service calls that keep coming back, point toward replacement. We say which case you are in and put the estimate in writing before work starts.
If the heat fails at night, (508) 786-8755 is answered around the clock. Our [maintenance page](/cities/chelmsford/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) covers the yearly check.

faq.q: Should I replace a working but old gas furnace in Chelmsford?
faq.a: Not automatically. If it runs safely and the bills are steady, a check and tune-up may be enough for a while. Replacement makes sense when repairs pile up, the heat exchanger is damaged or comfort is poor. We assess it before recommending anything.

faq.q: I heat with oil in Chelmsford. Can I switch to gas?
faq.a: Possibly, if a main serves your street and connecting is practical. Most of town heats with gas, yet that says nothing about your street, so availability has to be checked. A heat pump is the other route. We compare both for your address at the estimate.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Two thirds of Chelmsford homes are detached houses and a quarter sit in multi-unit buildings, so cooling options range from central air to ductless or per-unit systems. Summers are warm and humid, so sizing and moisture control matter.
body: ## Cooling a house, a townhouse or a unit in a big building

Two out of three Chelmsford homes are detached houses, but townhouses, mobile homes and multi-unit buildings make up the rest, and each cools differently. A detached house with sound ducts can often take a central system. A townhouse shares walls and can have less room outdoors. A unit on the third floor of a large building may have no duct space at all.
### Summers are warm and humid

Wikipedia describes the local climate as having warm, humid summers, and humidity is the part people feel in a stuffy bedroom. A correctly sized air conditioner removes moisture as well as heat. One that is too large cools quickly, shuts off and leaves the air clammy. Sizing starts with the house: the insulation, the windows, which way the roof faces and how many people live there.
### Houses from the boom decades

Many older homes were built before central air was common, and a town with a 1967 median build year has plenty of them. Hot-water heat means no ducts to reuse, so the choice is a new duct system or ductless mini-splits. Ductless heads mount on a wall, connect to an outdoor unit with a small line set and do not open up the walls.
### Checking the basics first

- Whether the electrical panel can take another circuit.
- Where an outdoor unit can sit without blocking a window, a walkway or a neighbor's fence.
- Which rooms actually run hot, since a whole-house system is not always needed.
### Condo and apartment owners

Owners in larger buildings usually have to follow the association's rules about outdoor equipment and noise, and some buildings limit what can be placed on balconies or roofs. We give you a written estimate so the board has something concrete to review.
### Repair or replace

A capacitor, a clogged drain line or a dirty coil is a repair. A compressor failure on an old unit, or a refrigerant leak on equipment that has already been recharged, usually tips toward replacement. We explain which it is in plain terms.
The [heat pump page](/cities/chelmsford/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers equipment that cools in summer and heats in winter.

faq.q: Can I add air conditioning to a Chelmsford house with hot-water heat?
faq.a: Yes. Without ducts, ductless mini-splits are the usual answer, with one indoor head per room or zone. A high-velocity duct system is another option in some houses. The layout and your budget decide which fits.

faq.q: How do I know what size air conditioner I need?
faq.a: It depends on the house, not just its square footage. Insulation, windows, shade and layout all matter. We calculate the load, because an oversized unit cools unevenly and leaves the air humid.

faq.q: Is a condo allowed to add an outdoor unit?
faq.a: That depends on the association's rules. Check the bylaws before ordering equipment. We can provide the written estimate and equipment details that a board will usually want to see.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: National Grid serves Chelmsford, where gas heats 76.1% of homes and oil only 9.6%. A heat pump here is more often about cooling and part of the load than about leaving oil, and only 9.6% of homes date from 2000 or later.
body: ## Heat pumps in a gas-heavy town

Heat pumps are usually sold as a way off oil or propane. Chelmsford has little of either: 1,303 homes burn oil and 349 use bottled gas, against 10,291 on utility gas. So the case here is different. A heat pump can add efficient cooling, replace baseboard electric heat or serve a room that the main system never heated well, and in some homes it makes sense alongside the gas furnace rather than in place of it.
### Utility and rebate, briefly

National Grid is the electric utility. Mass Save's 2026 whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton up to $8,500, and the house has to be weatherized first. Everything else is on our [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### How the age bands line up

Only 1,342 Chelmsford homes (9.6%) were built in 2000 or later, so for most owners the weatherization step is not settled by age alone. Another 3,112 homes (22.3%) date from 1980 to 1999, and 9,511 (68.1%) from before 1980. The largest band, 1960 to 1979, holds 5,123 homes (36.7%). In practice an energy assessment is where many Chelmsford heat pump projects begin.
### The 1,354 electric-heat homes

Electricity heats 1,354 homes (10.0%), slightly more than the 1,303 on oil. For a home with electric resistance heat, a heat pump is the natural comparison, since it moves heat instead of making it from scratch.
### Where a mini-split fits
- A finished attic, a sunroom or an addition on its own thermostat.
- One of the 2,834 homes in buildings of five or more units, where there may be no duct space.
- A house with hot-water heat that needs cooling.
- A bedroom that never matches the rest of the house.
### Whole home or partial

Keeping the gas furnace and adding a heat pump for mild weather is a partial-home setup, with the furnace as backup when it is very cold. Winters in Chelmsford are cold, windy and snowy according to Wikipedia, which is why that backup question comes up. See the [cooling page](/cities/chelmsford/air-conditioning-installation-repair) for the summer side.

faq.q: Is a heat pump worth it if I already heat with gas?
faq.a: It can be, mostly for cooling and shoulder seasons, and in some homes for replacing electric resistance heat. Whether it pays off depends on the house and the equipment. We go through the options at the estimate and do not promise savings.

faq.q: Will my Chelmsford home meet the weatherization condition?
faq.a: Only 9.6% of Chelmsford homes were built in 2000 or later, so most owners will need an assessment or finished recommendations to meet it. The main heat pump page lists the routes, and masssave.com has the current terms.

faq.q: Can a heat pump replace a gas furnace in Chelmsford?
faq.a: In some houses, yes, particularly where the load is modest. Many owners keep the furnace for the coldest days instead. With gas heating 76.1% of local homes, the comparison depends on the house, the ducts and what you want from the system, so we price the options side by side.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Gas heats most Chelmsford homes, so most visits are burner, venting and safety-control checks. The roughly one home in ten on oil has a yearly cleaning job too. Fall is the time for both, before the first hard cold.
body: ## A yearly check for gas equipment

Gas heat dominates Chelmsford, so a gas furnace or boiler is the most common system to service. A good visit covers the burner, the heat exchanger, the venting, the controls and the safety switches, with a combustion test where appropriate. It catches the quiet failures: a cracked part, a blocked flue, a filter that has not been changed in a year.
### Oil is a smaller group, but it needs more

The 1,303 oil homes (9.6%) are outnumbered by the 1,354 on electricity. An oil burner wants its cleaning once a year: nozzle, filter and combustion. Skip it and soot can build up until a working boiler becomes a no-heat call in January.
### Electric and heat pump systems
For the electric-heat homes and anyone with a heat pump, maintenance means coils, filters, drain lines and refrigerant-side checks. Outdoor units need clearance from leaves, snow and shrubs.
### Calendar
- **Early fall:** heating checks, ahead of the first cold stretch.
- **Late spring:** cooling checks on central air and mini-splits.
- **Any time:** noise, odor, short cycling or a bill that jumps.
### Old house, unknown equipment

The age of a house and the age of its equipment are different numbers. With 68.1% of Chelmsford homes built before 1980 and the median at 1967, the nameplate date is worth reading before anyone assumes anything. A tune-up also shows how much life a unit likely has left, and we would rather say so in writing than meet you on a freezing night.
### Landlords and associations

A shared boiler in one of the 5-plus-unit buildings (20.3% of homes) is a good candidate for a scheduled yearly visit, since a failure can reach every household at once. A check in early fall beats an emergency call in January.
### What to have ready
The fuel type, approximate age, make and model if visible, and what you have noticed. A photo of the nameplate helps. See also our [heating page](/cities/chelmsford/heating-installation-repair).

faq.q: How often should a gas furnace in Chelmsford be serviced?
faq.a: Once a year, ideally in early fall. In a town where gas heats 76.1% of homes, that is the norm, and the visit usually turns up small wear on the burner, venting or controls while it is still cheap to deal with.

faq.q: Do filters really need changing that often?
faq.a: Usually every one to three months for standard filters, depending on the type, pets and how much the system runs. A clogged filter cuts airflow, which strains the equipment and can lead to a shutdown.

faq.q: My Chelmsford house heats with oil. Is the yearly visit really necessary?
faq.a: It is the one service we would not skip for oil. Only about one home in ten here burns oil, so it is easy to forget, but nozzle, filter and combustion are the parts that decide whether the boiler starts on the first cold morning.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: More than a third of Chelmsford homes date from 1960 to 1979, and few are new. Leaky older houses and tighter renovated ones need different air solutions, starting with filters, humidity and ventilation.
body: ## Air in houses of the postwar boom

The median Chelmsford home dates to 1967, and age shapes the air inside. Homes from the 1960s and 1970s often leak through gaps around windows, rim joists and attic hatches. That lets stale air out and also lets in dust, pollen and damp basement air. A house tightened up with new windows and insulation saves energy but can hold moisture and cooking fumes inside.

### Which houses are tight
Newer homes usually leak less than older ones, so the 1,342 homes built in 2000 or later and the 3,112 from 1980 to 1999 are where ventilation deserves a second look. Only 3.8% of the town was built since 2010.
### Filters first

A better filter is the cheapest improvement, but only if the system can handle the extra resistance. A very dense filter in a system built for something thinner can cut airflow. We check the blower and ducts before recommending a higher rating, and we tell you how often to change it.
### Humidity

Summers here are warm and humid, and indoor air can turn dry in winter once the heat is on. Basements can be damp in summer and the rest of the house dry in January. A basement dehumidifier and a humidifier on the system can help, but a damp wall needs its source found first.
### Ventilation

- A bath fan that vents outdoors and actually runs.
- A range hood that exhausts to the outside.
- Fresh air supplied by an ERV or HRV in a very tight home.
- Dryer vents kept clear and ducted outdoors.
### Big buildings, shared air

About a quarter of Chelmsford's homes are in multi-unit buildings, where hallways, shared ducts and neighbors' cooking or smoke can affect the air in your unit. Air that travels between apartments is a building problem, and sealing and balancing often help more than a portable purifier.
### Duct cleaning, honestly
Cleaning ducts is not needed on a schedule. It can be worthwhile after a renovation, a pest problem or visible mold. We look first and tell you if it will help.
### When to test

Testing can show humidity, carbon monoxide or particles at a moment in time. It is a snapshot, so we use it to find a source, such as a leaking duct, an unvented appliance or a wet basement, and then fix the source.

faq.q: Will a higher-rated filter improve the air in my Chelmsford home?
faq.a: It can reduce dust and particles, but only if your system can move enough air through it. Check the equipment first. A clean filter matters as much as a high rating.

faq.q: Why is my basement damp every summer?
faq.a: Warm, humid air meets cool basement walls and condenses, or water enters from outside. A dehumidifier controls the air. A leak or poor grading has to be fixed at the source.

faq.q: Is a whole-house air purifier necessary?
faq.a: Usually not. Filters, ventilation and humidity control cover most homes. Purifiers can help people with particular sensitivities, and we can discuss the options without pushing equipment you do not need.
